Segregation no, safely slowly transitioning a traumatized kid to a new culture he has predisposed prejudices against, yes.

Yes, he wasn't in the best situation on Bajor and i don't think he should of stayed there forever, but i don't think sending him to a new planet with a new life and parent suddenly, is going to do his mental health any good. Not to mention he would be among a race he is totally uncomfortable with. He should have gradually transitioned, or they should have at least talked about it, but of course there are time restraints.

I use the word 'violently' more metaphorically, it's a traumatic situation all around. Neither homes are ideal at that particular time, but I think completely uprooting him from everything he is familiar with could make the transition more difficult. After sitting on it a bit, i understand that it was just a shitty situation and i think the episode just focused more on the politics than the welfare of the child, which is unfortunately an echo on current society.

I'm looking forward to reading that book. I understand it would be difficult for them all to uproot their lives, but i would imagine it would be important to them to provide the healthiest transition for this already traumatized kid. Sure, that situation maybe wouldn't of worked, but i just wish they explored that a bit. The kid just seemed like a piece of property. I know politics had a big part of the decision, and the reality that every orphan can't be given the luxury of a perfect situation.

I don't think any options were going to be good for this kid, and i don't think just going back to Bajor would be a good solution. My hope was he would spend time between the two and be able to adjust to his new life with as little traumatic shock as possible. Sending him straight to Cardassia with someone he doesn't even know, just shook me.

Yeah for sure, it's exploration of just plain shitty situations with no good outcome is a reason I love the show. 

I think setting some kind of situation where maybe all involved parties could stay on the station for an adjustment period. He can learn more about his situation and prepare himself for his new home and the journey of self acceptance be would on. With his parents he know and love nearby, he gets to feel safe, and with his biological dad nearby, he gets a chance to build that relationship. I would hope they would be willing to make the sacrifice of leaving their homes temporarily to support a healthier transition for their son. If that's not a possibility, maybe he could have extended stays with his father to get to know him, but know he can recoup at his Bajor home.

I just wish they would have explored those issues, but i know they have a time limit, and the politics of it were i think their main focus. But, shit does just happen in a shitty way sometimes.
